generation.mode: built-in ImageGen edit with edit-target as Image 1 and style canon as reference-only Image 2

lightingIsotropy.metric: 36-bin land-luminance-gradient magnitude peak divided by uniform-bin mean on the delivered source; mask water and its four immediate neighbours are excluded, as are gradients below 12 luminance units.
lightingIsotropy.visualCheck: No whole-cell sun gradient or cast-shadow field is visible, but the basalt columns repeatedly have pale caps over darker side faces and many conifers retain light-dark side modelling. The aggregate statistic does not establish the literal equal-value rule.

buildableVsSteepFraction.basis: Manual estimated fraction of non-water land area at native source resolution.
buildableVsSteepFraction.method: Broad coherent inland rock benches count as buildable; the immediate broken shore rim and incised upper stream banks count as steep; talus, shingle, stack rock, dense conifer groups, and rough margins make up the remainder. Approximate uncertainty is plus or minus 0.08 per fraction.

south.required: land except for the approximately 3 m arriving watercourse

crown.method: Manual outer-foliage width census of every visually distinguishable conifer crown, including saplings, dense-stand crowns, and edge-clipped crowns; native median 25.5 px scaled by 2560/1254 and converted at 4.8 cm per final pixel.

waterMask.encoding: Opaque white water pixels on fully transparent non-water pixels; binary alpha.
waterMask.componentNote: The main component is the open sea plus its source-visible upper stream reach. The second is the southern tarn and south-edge outflow. The separation records the generation's unintended dry break rather than inventing water not painted in the raw source.
waterMask.method: Flooded source-raster blue and teal from the open-sea edges, alternated bounded growth through adjacent pale surf and wash with connected wet-colour growth, separately traced the source-visible southern tarn and outflow through a cool-colour corridor, closed pixel-scale classifier gaps, and removed sub-16-pixel water speckles. Dry stacks and skerries remain transparent terrain.

refusalReasons: Land reaches both east and west edges; the brief requires those full edges to be open sea.
The generated watercourse is discontinuous: the upper reach connects to the sea, but a broad dry interval separates it from the southern tarn and south-edge outflow.
Only 23 source pixels, about 1.79 m at cell scale, are painted water on the south edge instead of the requested approximately 3 m arrival.

The island ground occupies substantially more of the frame than the requested shallow north-shore continuation and is dominated by broad open rock rather than dense dark forest with little open ground.
Repeated bright basalt caps over darker side faces and modelled conifer sides violate the literal neutral-lighting rule; several column runs also read too regular for ordinary weathered coast.
Several shore columns expose viewer-facing sides rather than reducing the north shore entirely to ground ending at a thin broken rim.
openRisks: The water mask follows the raw source rather than repairing its broken hydrology; downstream classification will therefore preserve two disconnected painted water components.
Buildable and steep fractions and the crown census are manual image measurements rather than surveyed geometry.
No second ImageGen call was made because the returned source was square and the task authorizes a retry only for non-square framing.
Seam continuity and overall visual quality remain director and owner judgments; this report does not claim visual acceptance.
